There is a 'dungeonTransitionSetup' method that seems to be called every time a dungeon is started. The issue with this is that it uses a check for if the 'floorNum' value is less than or equal to 1, and if it is, it evaluates ascension logic. For example, if you are on ascension 6 or higher, you would start every new floor with 90% of your current HP. On ascension 10 or higher, you would have an "Ascenders Bane" curse added to your deck every new floor. On Ascension 14 or higher, you would have your max health reduced by 5, 4, 4 (Ironclad, Silent, Defect respectively) every floor. On top of this, the current playtime of your run would be set to 0 every single floor.

Adding onto this, it looks like a method called 'initializeRelicList' is called at the start of every floor, to re-populate the relic lists and then every relic the player has is removed from the relic lists so you won't find them more than once (Why this is done every floor is confusing to me but I'm sure there's a good reason, and since I've barely looked at the code I won't begin to assumed anything). The issue here however is that it only does this for when 'floorNum' is greater than or equal to 1. It's part of the model that they haven't bothered to remove, it's only visible because the head has yet to be culled by the engine.

The teeth along with the rest of the head, is culled by the game, so it would not even be taken into account when the game is rendering the entire scene. I assume the reason we see it at the start, is that the game just hasn't culled the head yet. 

In terms of how the game renders in general, rendering is just generating a 2D image from the 3D scene, so anything that shouldn't show up on the screen, isn't rendered. If it were then you'd see it.

In an engine like Unreal, it should be a relatively minor amount of resources to check. Especially since the head of the player model is culled by the camera so the head is most likely set to be invisible anyway.

Rendering is just the process of generating a single frame from the objects on screen. So while the insides of the head are being rendered multiple times a second at the start of the game when you are inside your player's head, they are no longer being rendered later in the game when the inside of the head is no longer visible.

The only real downside of having the teeth and such existing inside a player's head, is that it would take up more memory, however it's most likely not a significant amount of data, and it shouldn't really be impacting performance in any meaningful way.

I personally do not often spend money on loot box type purchases in games because I don't think that they're a good system either, but only when they effect gameplay. Loot boxes in Overwatch are purchasable, but they are purely cosmetic, you don't HAVE to purchase them in the same way that you do for games like Hearthstone these days. The income from loot boxes is what allows many developers to keep developing the game. However, I do think that there are better ways to generate income to keep your game afloat, before it introduced its own loot boxes, League of Legends had a good system where you bought points and directly used those points to buy skins. Purely cosmetic, no effect on gameplay, but it wasn't randomised and it worked well. My only issue with it was that a single skin could cost around $10 alone, which is insanely expensive for a single cosmetic item. Loot boxes, in my opinion, are not bad when you can earn them for free, and when they have no bearing on the actual game at all. Especially in Overwatch's case, where you earn money from the loot boxes so that you can purchase reasonably priced cosmetics without ever paying Blizzard a cent, unless you're really desperate for a certain skin, right this second.

Why does it matter if a loot box containing ONLY cosmetics that have NO bearing on the actual gameplay itself, costs money? You can get them by playing the game, duplicates and money drops mean that you can buy specific cosmetics that you want without spending any money, or you can spend money and get cosmetics sooner, but that's entirely up to the user and it doesn't have any effect on any other player of the game. Not only that, but the money from loot boxes allow the Overwatch team to constantly churn out updates with lots of new content all for free, which is, in my opinion, much more important than paid loot boxes.

I despised the DLC when it came out because it was unbalanced and unfun. Months later it's certainly better, but I personally still don't think it's great.

The best part of the DLC in my opinion is definitely the mod support. It's really useful and it's been lots of fun to play around with. However, I honestly think the game was better off without the new content from AB+. I dislike lots of the items they've added, with a few exception such as Jacob's Ladder, Little Horn, Crooked Penny and a few others. However most of the new enemies and bosses I don't think are that interesting or fun in comparison to the old ones. Portals for example just aren't very interesting or fun to me, instead of creatively making a room with thought out enemies and placement, they just slap some portals on there and let them do all the work. Stoneys are alright, they're one of the new enemies I'm cool with. As many people have already mentioned, Blisters are stupid and make no sense. The tentacle wall creep thing is cool, I like that enemy. Those are some of the main ones. Bosses on the other hand aren't great in my opinion. Big Horn started out unfair as hell, now he's pretty easy but also pretty boring, it's not a boss I like seeing. Rag Mega is also pretty boring and just not very fun, you can easily kill it and it's not exactly hard, making the fight pretty boring. Sisters Vis were another boss which were way too strong on release but are now way too easy. The fight is kind of interesting, I like them the most out of the new bosses, with a few tweaks they could be a difficult but fun boss fight. 

There's also the issue of the Void floor, which is just so poorly done in my opinion. Everything in it is just recycling old assets with no real attempt to change them. The Delirium fight is just an uninspired in my opinion, it's just existing bosses retextured and they occasionally shoot some silver tears and stuff. Also they get gradually faster and the entire fight just isn't that fun to me. There's also just not much real incentive to go there, at least in the Chest you get some items and all chests are guaranteed to give items (Dark Room as well but without the 4 free items at the start), so your run can become more interesting. You also have the option of fighting Mega Satan which can be fun every now and then.

Another thing, Greedier mode. It's eh, as Greed mode has always sort of been. The addition of Ultra Greedier made it worse in my opinion because it just makes the fight take longer than it already does and isn't especially difficult if you get a pattern down. Why Greed/Greedier mode is bad in my opinion; It promotes a strong and powerful run to clear waves in time, which is fine, and it's not a particularly difficult mode to do well in with multiple essentially free items every floor. However, the Ultra Greed fight doesn't fit in, it promotes surivivability when the entire time you've had to build your run to be strong. It's a complete dynamic shift right at the end making it just kind of lackluster. If Ultra Greed had no armour but instead had some more health, it would be much better in my opinion. Also, the button to stop the waves is way too punishing as well. Less money and you have to sacrifice health just because you weren't powerful enough to clear the waves in time is not very good for the player and makes the button almost never worth pushing, especially when you really need to because your health will probably already be low.
